summary: Suspected phishing led to unusual service-account access; privilege scope review requested
description:
Issue summary: On 2026-03-12 at ~09:18 UTC Security received an automated phishing report (security-phish-reporting@) referencing a credential-reset link sent to a small set of employees. Shortly after, Okta sign-in alerts flagged an atypical successful sign-in for the service account 'infra-deploy@redwood.ai' from an IP with a suspicious geolocation. This ticket captures the triage and containment steps for a suspected phishing-triggered service-account access attempt.

Detection: Automated phish mailbox + Okta adaptive auth alert + deployment pipeline audit spike.

Primary questions: Was the service account actually used to run deployments or access secrets? How did the phish lure map to a token/credential used by the service account? Is there lateral movement?
impact: Potential privilege escalation affecting deployment pipelines and access to secret metadata. No confirmed production data exfiltration or destructive deployments found at time of last update, but elevated risk remains while the service account remained active.
detected_by: security-phish-reporting@redwood.ai and Okta security alert (suspicious geolocation)
timeline:
2026-03-12 09:12 UTC - Phish report received.
2026-03-12 09:18 UTC - Okta alert: successful sign-in for infra-deploy@ from anonymized IP (suspected foreign ASN).
2026-03-12 09:22 UTC - Deployment pipeline recorded an auth token refresh for infra-deploy@ (no deployment kicked).
2026-03-12 09:27 UTC - Security notified SRE and token rotation initiated.
2026-03-12 10:05 UTC - Service account disabled and active sessions revoked.
2026-03-12 11:30 UTC - Initial log sweep completed; no destructive actions observed.
steps_to_reproduce: N/A - incident response / forensics task. Reproduction not applicable (spear-phish social engineering vector).
logs: Okta event IDs: evt-99827, evt-99828 indicating successful MFA bypass attempt then normal sign-in. Deployment auth logs show token refresh event id tok-20260312-44 with caller infra-deploy@. Secrets-manager access log shows a single metadata read (redacted) at 09:23 UTC from same token. No large secret bulk reads. Full raw logs stored in s3://sec-logs/2026-03-12/okta/ and s3://sec-logs/2026-03-12/deploy/ (access by Security/SRE only).
investigation_notes:
Hypotheses: (1) Targeted phishing link harvested credentials for a human admin who then triggered a flow that allowed service account token refresh; (2) Service account credentials were stored in an accessible place and were exposed via phishing link.

What we've checked: Okta session history for infra-deploy@, recent GitHub secrets changes, CI secret rotations, KMS audit logs, ECR push history, and S3 object access patterns. No code push or deployments occurred using that token. KMS logs show no CMK decrypts by the account outside a single small metadata read.

Open investigative tasks: full memory snapshot of runner that requested token (POC: infra-runner-18), forensics on host that triggered token refresh, correlate phishing recipient list with recent admin sessions.
actions_taken:
1) Disabled infra-deploy@ service account and revoked all its API tokens and active sessions (09:27 UTC).
2) Forced rotation of related CI secrets and rotated keys in secrets-manager.
3) Blocked the suspicious IP ranges at perimeter and added to blocklist (temporary).
4) Increased Okta adaptive MFA requirement for high-privilege roles and added an immediate MFA re-evaluation policy.
5) Notified Legal and CISO team; created a hold on potential affected artifacts for forensic preservation.
resolution: Containment completed: service account disabled, tokens rotated, and immediate risk mitigations applied. No confirmed data theft or destructive action detected. Case remains 'Monitoring' pending deeper host forensics and confirmation of the phishing vector. Next steps include root-cause verification, full credential inventory, and an org-wide targeted phishing awareness email with recommended mitigations.
